questions.title: James-Stein shrinkage for a multivariate normal mean
questions.description: Focused known-result evaluation based on W. James and Charles Stein, Estimation with Quadratic Loss, Proceedings of the Fourth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability, Volume 1, 1961, pages 361-379. Let X be distributed as N_p(theta, sigma^2 I_p), where p is at least 3 and sigma^2 is known and positive, and use total squared-error loss. In an authoritative Markdown/LaTeX theory workspace, derive rather than merely quote that the usual estimator delta_0(X)=X has constant risk p sigma^2. For the ordinary, untruncated James-Stein estimator delta_JS(X) = (1 - (p-2)sigma^2/||X||^2)X, derive the Stein-identity risk calculation and the exact risk reduction R(theta,delta_JS)=p sigma^2-(p-2)^2 sigma^4 E_theta[1/||X||^2] < p sigma^2. Make the divergence calculation, integrability for p greater than 2, uniformity in theta, and the probability-zero singularity at X=0 auditable. Distinguish this ordinary estimator from the positive-part estimator and explain why the p=1 or p=2 cases are outside the stated dominance result. The required algorithm artifact id is est_james_stein_normal_mean. Its run_estimator(request) input has observations as one nonzero length-p numeric array with p at least 3 and known_variance as a positive numeric scalar. It must return estimate as a length-p numeric array and shrinkage_factor as a numeric scalar for the ordinary, untruncated estimator. State a finite numerical policy for the exact-zero input without changing the almost-sure statistical result. Use exploratory computation only as a diagnostic, then run a separately frozen confirmatory paired Monte Carlo comparison of squared-error risk across multiple predeclared dimensions and signal strengths, reporting Monte Carlo standard errors. This L0 task exposes the known result, source snapshot, and ABI; it tests faithful derivation, implementation, empirical validation, and honest gaps rather than novelty. Source-code replication and Lean formalization are not applicable.
